minutes_text:
Tuesday Meeting of the
  City of Huntington Park City Council
  Tuesday, June 23, 2026

 The regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Huntington Park, California was
 called to order at 6:08 p.m. on Tuesday, June 23, 2026, in the Council Chambers at City
 Hall, 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California; Mayor Eduardo “Eddie” Martinez
 presiding.

 PRESENT: Council Member(s): Martiz, Macias, Vice Mayor Sanabria, and Mayor
 Martinez

 ABSENT: Council Member(s): Flores

 CITY OFFICIALS/STAFF: Eduardo Sarmiento City Clerk; Louis Morales Interim
 Community Development Director; Cosme Lozano Chief of Police; Jeff Jones Finance
 Director, Gerardo “Gerry” Lopez Public Works Director; Cynthia Norzagaray Parks and Recreation
 Director; Andrew Sarega City Attorney; Karina Ruedas Human Resources Director;
 Stephany Santin Assistant City Manager; and Ricardo Reyes City Manager.

INVOCATION
 Invocation was led by Mayor Martinez

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
 Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Sanabria.

PRESENTATION(S)

 1.  UNHOUSED REPORT AND ACTIVITY UPDATE

 PUBLIC COMMENTS

  1. Carlyn Bartellet- Mexico World Cup Complaints/ 4th of July Event.
  2. David Sanchez- Noise + Pollution in Community
  3. Rudy Cruz
  4. Manuel Martinez

  CONSENT CALENDAR
CITY CLERK

1.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:
  Approve Minute(s) of the following City Council Meeting(s):
  1. Regular City Council Meeting June 9, 2026
FINANCE

2.  WARRANT REGISTERS

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Approve Accounts Payable and Payroll Warrant(s) dated June 18, 2026

PUBLIC WORKS

3.  RESOLUTION TO APPROVE ADOPTING A LIST OF PROJECTS FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2026-27 FUNDED BY SENATE BILL 1 (SB1), THE ROAD REPAIR AND
  ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Adopt Resolution approving the Fiscal Year 2026-27 project list for Senate Bill 1
  (SB1), the Road Repair and Accountability Act of 2017; and
   2. Authorize staff to upload the resolution with the list of streets to the California
  Transportation Commission (CTC) website, Cal SMART.

  MOTION:  Councilmember Martiz motioned to approve the consent calendar in
  its entirety. The motion was seconded by Vice Mayor Sanabria.
  Councilmember Macias abstained from voting on the motion. The
  motion was carried by majority vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s) Martiz, Vice Mayor Sanabria and Mayor
  Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): Macias

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Flores

  END OF CONSENT CALENDAR

  ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

CITY MANAGER

1.  CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF RESOLUTIONS RELATED TO THE CITY
  OF HUNTINGTON PARK’S GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION AND SPECIAL
  MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO BE HELD TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 3, 2026

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Adopt a Resolution calling for the Holding of a General Municipal Election and a
  Special Municipal Election to be held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, for the
  Election of Certain Officers, and Requesting the Board of Supervisors of the
  County of Los Angeles to Consolidate the Elections with the Statewide General
  Election also called to be held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and Requesting
  the Board to Render Specified Services to the City Relating to the Conduct of
  Said Elections; and

  2. Adopt a Resolution adopting regulations for candidates for elective office
  pertaining to candidates’ statements submitted to the voters at an election to be
  held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026; and

  3. Adopt a Resolution providing for the conduct of a special runoff election for
  elective offices in the event of a tie vote at any municipal election.

  MOTION: Vice Mayor Sanabria motioned to adopt a resolution calling for the holding
  of a General Municipal Election and a Special Municipal Election to be held on
  Tuesday, November 3, 2026, for the Election of Certain Officers, and Requesting the
  Board of Supervisors of the County of Los Angeles to consolidate the elections with
  the Statewide General Election also called to be held on Tuesday, November 3,
  2026, and Requesting the Board to Render Specified Services to the City Relating
  to the conduct of said elections; adopt a resolution adopting regulations for
  candidates for elective office pertaining to candidates’ statements submitted to the
  voters at an election to be held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026; and adopt a
  resolution providing for the conduct of a special runoff election for elective offices in
  the event of a tie vote at any municipal election. The motion was seconded by
  Councilmember Martiz. Councilmember Macias voted against the motion. The
  motion was carried by majority vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Vice Mayor Sanabria and Mayor
  Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): Macias

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): None
   ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Flores

2.  CONSIDERATION OF AUTHORIZING THE RELEASE OF A REQUEST FOR
  QUALIFICATIONS (RFQ) FOR A HYBRID PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP (P3)
  OPERATING PARTNER FOR THE CITY’S MUNICIPALLY OWNED BROADBAND
  ENTERPRISE RECOMMENDATION

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Affirm the City's policy direction to retain municipal ownership, governance, and
  strategic control of the City's broadband infrastructure through a municipally
  owned broadband enterprise leveraging a hybrid public-private partnership (P3)
  operating model; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to issue a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) to identify
  qualified firms capable of operating and supporting the City's broadband network
  consistent with this policy direction; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to subsequently issue a Request for Proposals (RFP)
  to qualified firms identified through the RFQ process; and

  4. Direct the City Manager to negotiate a proposed operating agreement and return
  to the City Council for approval prior to execution.

  MOTION: Vice Mayor Sanabria motioned to affirm the city's policy direction to retain
  municipal ownership, governance, and strategic control of the city's broadband
  infrastructure through a municipally owned broadband enterprise leveraging a hybrid
  public-private partnership (P3) operating model; authorize the City Manager to issue
  a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) to identify qualified firms capable of operating
  and supporting the City's broadband network consistent with this policy direction;
  and authorize the City Manager to subsequently issue a Request for Proposals
  (RFP) to qualified firms identified through the RFQ process; and direct the City
  Manager to negotiate a proposed operating agreement and return to the City Council
  for approval prior to execution. Councilmember Martiz seconded the motion.
  Councilmember Macias asked that we reference Culver City’s RFQ for Municipally
  owned Broadband Enterprise. The motion was carried by majority vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Macias, Vice Mayor Sanabria and
  Mayor Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Flores

COMMUNICATIONS AND COMMUNITY RELATIONS

3.  APPROVAL AND ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION ADOPTING AN OFFICIAL
  DIGITAL MEDIUMS PRIVACY POLICY AND TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF USE
  FOR CITY ONLINE SERVICES, COMMUNICATION CHANNELS, AND MOBILE
  APPLICATIONS

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Adopt a Resolution approving the City of Huntington Park Digital Mediums Privacy
  Policy and Terms & Conditions of Use for City online services, communication
  channels, and mobile applications.

  MOTION:  Vice Mayor Sanabria motioned to adopt a resolution approving the City
  of Huntington Park Digital Mediums Privacy Policy and Terms &
  Conditions of Use for City online services, communication channels,
  and mobile applications. The motion was seconded by Councilmember
  Martiz. The motion was carried by majority vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Macias, Vice Mayor Sanabria and
   Mayor Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Flores

PUBLIC WORKS

4.  CONSIDERATION OF APPROVAL TO AWARD A CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT
  FOR CIP 2022-12 WATER QUALITY GREEN STREETS PROJECT

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Award the construction contract to Excel Paving Company for the construction of
  CIP 2022-12 Water Quality Green Streets Project for the not-to-exceed amount
  of $1,572,898; and

  2. Approve a 20% construction contingency in the amount of $314,580, 10% project
  management and inspection in the amount of $157,290, and labor compliance in
  the amount of $17,970; and

  3. Adopt a resolution awarding a construction contract for CIP 2022-12 Water
  Quality Green Streets Project; and

  4. Authorize the City Manager to execute the construction contract agreement and
  all change orders in good faith; and

  5. Staff recommend City Council adopt the resolution to award a construction
  contract for CIP 2022-12 Water Quality Green Streets Project.

  MOTION:  Vice Mayor Sanabria motioned to award the construction contract to
  Excel Paving Company for the construction of CIP 2022-12 Water
  Quality Green Streets Project for the not-to-exceed amount of
  $1,572,898; approve a 20% construction contingency in the amount
  of $314,580, 10% project management and inspection in the amount
  of $157,290, and labor compliance in the amount of $17,970; adopt a
  resolution awarding a construction contract for CIP 2022-12 Water
  Quality Green Streets Project; authorize the City Manager to execute
  the construction contract agreement and all change orders in good
  faith; and adopt the resolution staff recommended to award a
  construction contract for CIP 2022-12 Water Quality Green Streets
  Project. Mayor Martinez seconded the motion. The motion was
  carried by majority vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Macias, Vice Mayor Sanabria and
  Mayor Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Flores

5.  CONSIDERATION OF APPROVAL TO AWARD A CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT
  FOR CIP 2022-11 LITTER ABATEMENT AND BEAUTIFICATION PROJECT

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Award the construction contract to Ace Capital Engineering for the construction
  of CIP 2022-11 Litter Abatement and Beautification Project for the not-to-exceed
  amount of $1,183,650.02; and

  2. Approve a 20% construction contingency in the amount of $236,730, 10% project
  management and inspection in the amount of $118,365, and labor compliance in
  the amount of $15,330; and
   3. Adopt a resolution awarding a construction contract for CIP 2022-11 litter
  abatement and beautification project; and

  4. Authorize the City Manager to execute the construction contract agreement and
  all change orders in good faith; and

  5. Staff recommend City Council adopt the resolution to award a construction
  contract for CIP 2022-11 Litter Abatement and Beautification Project.

  MOTION:  Mayor Martinez motioned to award the construction contract to Ace
  Capital Engineering for the construction of CIP 2022-11 Litter
  Abatement and Beautification Project for the not-to-exceed amount of
  $1,183,650.02; approve a 20% construction contingency in the
  amount of $236,730, 10% project management and inspection in the
  amount of $118,365, and labor compliance in the amount of $15,330;
  adopt a resolution awarding a construction contract for CIP 2022-11
  litter abatement and beautification project; authorize the City Manager
  to execute the construction contract agreement and all change orders
  in good faith; adopt the resolution to award a construction contract for
  CIP 2022-11 Litter Abatement and Beautification Project; Authorize
  the City Manager to execute the construction contract agreement and
  all change orders in good faith; and adopt the staff recommended
  resolution to award a construction contract for CIP 2022-11 Litter
  Abatement and Beautification Project. Councilmember Martiz
  seconded the motion. The motion was carried by majority vote. The
  motion was carried by majority vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Macias, Vice Mayor Sanabria and
  Mayor Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Flores

6.  CONSIDERATION OF APPROVAL TO AWARD A CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT
  FOR PUBLIC WORKS YARD ROOF REPLACEMENT

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Award the construction contract to Letner Roofing Company for the construction
  of the Public Works Yard Roof Replacement for the not-to-exceed amount of
  $391,490; and

  2. Adopt a resolution for the approval to award a construction contract for public
  works yard roof replacement; and

  3. Approve a 30% construction contingency in the amount of $117,447, and 10%
  project management and inspection in the amount of $39,149

  MOTION:  Vice Mayor Sanabria motioned to award the construction contract to
  Letner Roofing Company for the construction of the Public Works Yard
  Roof Replacement for the not-to-exceed amount of $391,490; adopt a
  resolution for the approval to award a construction contract for public
  works yard roof replacement; and approve a 30% construction
  contingency in the amount of $117,447, and 10% project management
  and inspection in the amount of $39,149. Councilmember Martiz
  seconded the motion. The motion was carried by majority vote.
  .

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Macias, Vice Mayor Sanabria and
  Mayor Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): None
   ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Flores

POLICE DEPARTMENT

7.  CONSIDERATION OF ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION ESTABLISHING
  UPDATED ADMINISTRATIVE FINES FOR VIOLATIONS OF CHAPTER 20 OF
  TITLE 4 OF THE HUNTINGTON PARK MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO
  FIREWORKS

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Adopt a Resolution establishing updated administrative fines for fireworks.

  MOTION:  Vice Mayor Sanabria motioned to adopt a resolution establishing
  updated administrative fines for fireworks. Mayor Martinez seconded
  the motion. The motion was carried by majority vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Macias, Vice Mayor Sanabria and
  Mayor Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Flores

HUMAN RESOURCES

8. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF A RESOLUTION APPROVING REVISIONS
  TO THE CLASS SPECIFICATION FOR THE POSITION OF CITY CLERK

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:
  1. Adopt a Resolution of the City Council of the City of Huntington Park Approving
  Revisions to the Class Specification for the Position of City Clerk

  MOTION:  Vice Mayor Sanabria motioned to adopt a resolution of the City Council
  of the City of Huntington Park Approving Revisions to the Class
  Specification for the Position of City Clerk. Councilmember Martiz
  seconded the motion. Councilmember Macias abstained from voting
  on the motion. The motion was carried by majority vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Vice Mayor Sanabria and Mayor Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): Macias

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Flores

  END OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  REPORTS AND INFORMATIONAL ITEMS

COMMUNICATIONS AND COMMUNITY RELATIONS

1.  APPROVAL OF A ONE-YEAR EXTENSION OF THE HP WITH YOU COMMUNITY
  RESILIENCE PILOT INITIATIVE AND THE FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE
  CONTRACT SERVICES AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF HUNTINGTON
  PARK AND SOUTHEAST LEADERSHIP NETWORK TO CONTINUE
  IMPLEMENTING THE “HP WITH YOU” COMMUNITY RESILIENCE PILOT
  INITIATIVE

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:
   1. Approve a one-year extension of the HP With You Community Resilience Pilot
  Initiative for Fiscal Year 2026-2027; and

  2. Approve First Amendment to Contract Services Agreement between the City of
  Huntington Park and Southeast Leadership Network for administration and
  implementation of the HP With You Initiative through June 30, 2027, in an amount
  not to exceed $150,000.

  MOTION:  Vice Mayor Sanabria motion to approve a one-year extension of the HP
  With You Community Resilience Pilot Initiative for Fiscal Year 2026-
  2027; and approve First Amendment to Contract Services Agreement
  between the City of Huntington Park and Southeast Leadership
  Network for administration and implementation of the HP With You
  Initiative through June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $150,000.
  Councilmember Martiz seconded the motion. The motion was carried
  by majority vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Macias, Vice Mayor Sanabria and
  Mayor Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Flores

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

2.  CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL TO AWARD FY26-27 MEASURE A FUNDS
  TO THE SALVATION ARMY BELL SHELTER AS THE SUBRECIPEINT TO
  PROVIDE UNHOUSED SERVICES

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Award a One (1) year subrecipient agreement to provide homeless
  services by The Salvation Army Bell Shelter for the not-to-exceed
  amount of $194,910; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Subrecipient agreement.

  MOTION:  Vice Mayor Sanabria motioned to award a One (1) year
  subrecipient agreement to provide homeless services by The
  Salvation Army Bell Shelter for the not-to-exceed amount of
  $194,910; and authorized the City Manager to execute the
  Subrecipient agreement. Councilmember Martiz seconded the
  motion. Councilmember Macias abstained from voting on the
  motion. The motion was carried by majority vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Flores, Vice Mayor Sanabria and
  Mayor Martinez

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): Macias

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

  END OF REPORTS AND INFORMATIONAL ITEMS

  DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS

Finance: No Report

City Manager: No Report
 City Attorney: No Report.

Police: For June 24th FIFA game, we will be in communication with Mutual Aid to conduct
crowd control and contain activities that might get out of control. There will be limit
passing capacity on Pacific Blvd temporarily during and post the soccer game.

City Clerk: Nothing to report.

Parks and Recreation: The city will be safely celebrating at a watch party scheduled at
Guajillo’s restaurant on Wednesday, June 24th and La Casita on Thursday, June 25th. We
would also like everyone to join us on Thursday, July 2nd for the Independence Day
celebration drone show and celebration.

Community Development: No Report.

Public Works: No Report

Communication: On Thursday, June 25th we will be a Pacific partners’ meeting at
Guajillo’s restaurant. On Thursday, June 25th, we will also be hosting a “Coffee with a
Cop” event at the Starbucks inside of Target on Randolph. On July 2nd, we will be hosting
a drone show for the Independence Day celebration. Services at City Hall will be
relocated to modular buildings behind City Hall on July 6th. All City Council Meetings, and
City Commission meetings will also be moved to Raul Perez Park until the end of the City
Hall remodel.

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS

Councilmember Martiz: I wanted to share about this weekend it was very beautiful
seeing the community event in our neighboring city. It was nice seeing the open street
events and the people of the community and local communities coming out. Want to see
about partnering with the neighbors. This was a reminder of local hazards such as the
Boyle Heights fire. Thinking about the 4th of July event wanted to see what staff can do
to ensure that members of the public are safe.

Councilmember Macias: Thank you to everybody! I wanted to bring up some concerns
regarding staff at the watch parties and want to ensure staff are behaving as public
servants. Make sure certain activities are monitored and staff behave appropriately and
safely.

Vice Mayor Sanabria: Thank you everybody. Requested update on the conversation
Janice Hahn had in regard to the Boyle Heights fire and requested that City Manager
gives a report [Assistant City Manager Stephany Santin gave a summary report: Air
quality has improved, and communications were sent out to the public].

Mayor Martinez: Thank you staff for making sure we have a successful event at Raul
Perez Park. Thank you to staff for assisting with the community events. If we could host
an open community event ourselves, maybe at Salt Lake Park it would be appreciated.
He also wanted to add a Study Session about the My Huntington Park App, particularly
the bulky pickup item. Lately, they are not being picked up.

  CLOSED SESSION

  None

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  None

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION: Mayor Martinez adjourned the meeting at 9:18pm. The next regular city council
meeting is set to be held on Tuesday, July 14th, 2026 @6pm at Raul Perez Park.
 Respectfully submitted,

Eduardo Sarmiento, City Clerk
